title: Modifying Dysfunctional Cognitions to Address Fear of Headache Attacks and Headache-Related Burden in Cluster Headache: A Randomized Controlled Trial
summary: Cluster headache is a relatively rare but very severe condition that can have a major impact on people’s lives and is often associated with mental health problems. This impact can extend beyond the headache attacks, with many people experiencing significant difficulties between attacks. However, it is still unclear which psychological factors contribute to these difficulties. This study examines whether an individualized, computer-based psychological intervention can help people change unhelpful thoughts about pain and, in turn, reduce fear of headache attacks and other headache-related difficulties.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Reported cluster headache diagnosis and validated using the ICHD-3 criteria
Exclusion criteria:
Revoking the declartion of consent; drug-/ alcohol consumption; uncorrected visual or hearing impairment; psychotic symptoms; cognitive disorders that negatively affect learning
